_note: Descriptions authored by reading each extracted image with a vision model. 'type' distinguishes true clinical films from screenshots of reference text (Orthobullets/journal) that residents pasted as evidence. 'tested_topic' is what the associated question was probing, so the topic is recoverable without the question stem.

image1.png.description: Humeral shaft fracture fixed with dual (orthogonal/parallel) plates; annotation points to gapping at the far cortex / fracture site.
image1.png.tested_topic: Humeral shaft fracture dual-plate fixation – technical error causing fracture-site gapping (compression/reduction technique)

image2.jpg.modality: Sagittal lumbar spine MRI (T1 and post-contrast/T2), two panels
image2.jpg.description: L4 vertebral body lesion with endplate/marrow signal change (arrowhead + arrow); paraspinal/epidural involvement. In context of sepsis + LBP + UTI, pattern of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis/discitis.
image2.jpg.tested_topic: Vertebral osteomyelitis / discitis – MRI diagnosis vs metastasis in the septic patient

image3.png.modality: Journal article excerpt (OTA Highlight Paper, JOT)
image3.png.description: Screenshot of Ihejirika-Lomedico et al. RCT on intraoperative local pain-cocktail (HiFI) injections in hip fracture surgery – results paragraph highlighting reduced pain/narcotic use and fewer complications.
image3.png.tested_topic: Peri-articular local anaesthetic (pain cocktail) injection in hip fracture – evidence for reduced pain/opioids

image4.png.description: Lumbar disc herniation location-classification question with MRI + dermatome figure; teaching point that L4-L5 paracentral herniation compresses the traversing L5 root.
image4.png.tested_topic: Lumbar disc herniation – paracentral vs foraminal and which nerve root is affected

image5.png.description: Bulleted reference: posterolateral/paracentral herniation (90-95%, affects traversing root; L4/5 → L5) vs foraminal/far-lateral (5-10%, affects exiting root; L4/5 → L4).
image5.png.tested_topic: Lumbar disc herniation – paracentral vs far-lateral nerve-root involvement

image6.png.description: Rheumatoid wrist 'radiocarpal destruction' pathoanatomy bullets: synovitis → ulnar/volar carpal translocation, scaphoid flexion, radioscaphoid arthrosis, ulnar finger drift (zigzag deformity).
image6.png.tested_topic: Rheumatoid wrist – pattern of radiocarpal destruction / carpal translocation

image7.jpg.description: Knee radiographs with arrows (A-D) labelling structures/findings (tibial spines/eminence and joint-line features).
